clue.text: Goes to nurse in war-time service

indicators.note: the nursing word is placed inside the abbreviation for the wartime service

parts.note: ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone leaves home to work as a nurse in a wartime women's corps.
explanation.walkthrough: ATS is the Auxiliary Territorial Service, Britain's wartime women's army corps; TEND goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to a school or meeting regularly is to be present there, a straight synonym.

clue.text: No marks for such wild shooting

definitions.text: No marks for such wild shooting

parts.words: No marks for such wild shooting
parts.note: shooting without taking aim at any target, read as lacking aim

explanation.surface: A judge awards no points to a marksman firing wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and it says the shooting is without aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Without purpose or direction, literally lacking a target to shoot at.

clue.text: Soon confounded in, test of shaving

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Muddled soon after starting a shaving test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' scrambles SOON into ONSO, which 'in' puts inside TRIAL after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers or hairdressing, including shaving.

clue.text: Poor marshal outflanks journalist

indicators.note: outflanks means goes round both sides, so the marshal surrounds the journalist

parts.note: Michel Ney, one of Napoleon's marshals
ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: A poor military commander's flanks are turned by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal Ney was one of Napoleon's commanders; NEY goes round ED, the usual abbreviation for an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means lacking money, so in want, poverty-stricken.

clue.text: Various articles for philosophers' drinks party

definitions.meaning: a collection of essays by different writers on one subject
in ancient Greece a drinking party with talk, as in Plato's dialogue

explanation.walkthrough: Plato's dialogue of that name is set at an Athenian drinking party where the guests discuss love.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of papers by several contributors; originally a Greek banquet with drinking and debate.

clue.text: Furs from upset cats, for instance

parts.note: to upset a vase is to tip it over
cats are an example of household pets

explanation.surface: Fur stoles made from the coats of distressed cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tippets are capes or stoles, traditionally made of fur, worn about the shoulders.

clue.text: Their ups and downs are ungovernable, the old king showed

definitions.text: Their ups and downs are ungovernable, the old king showed

parts.words: Their ups and downs are ungovernable, the old king showed
parts.note: refers to King Canute, who set his throne on the shore to show his courtiers he could not command the sea to stop rising

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch demonstrated that some rises and falls cannot be controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: The old king is Canute, who showed his flatterers that the sea would not obey him.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising and falling of the sea, which no ruler can command.

clue.text: This way was made to last

definitions.text: This way was made to last

parts.words: This way was made to last
parts.note: railway track, with its rails and sleepers, is known as the way that is built to endure

explanation.surface: A road built to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: The permanent way is the railway track bed, rails and sleepers: built to last.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever or for a long time; with 'way' after it, the British name for a railway track.

clue.text: Come on stage in magnificent ermine

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An actor makes an entrance dressed in splendid royal fur.
explanation.definitionFit: To come on stage is to make an entrance, a theatrical synonym.

clue.text: Got lost, once you entered the return game?

indicators.note: entered means the old pronoun goes inside the turned game
return means the game word is read backwards

parts.note: darts is a pub game
ye, an old form of you

explanation.surface: A player wandered off after joining in the second match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns DARTS into STRAD; 'entered' puts YE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the right path, so to go astray.

clue.text: Scholar has points in the House for the Minister

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a scholar's degree
N, S and E are points of the compass

explanation.surface: An academic brings up points of order in Parliament addressed to the Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' and 'Minister' suggest Parliament, but this minister is a clergyman, chiefly a Scottish Presbyterian one.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the residence provided for a Presbyterian or other Nonconformist clergyman.

clue.text: Ecclesiastic eminence after a Russian order's retreat

indicators.note: after puts the hill word at the end, following the turned pieces
retreat means go backwards, so the run of three pieces before it is read from the end

parts.note: a Russian is called a Red, from Soviet communism
OM, the Order of Merit, a British honour
a tor is a rocky hill, an eminence

explanation.surface: A church dignitary of high rank follows the withdrawal of a Russian religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns A + RED + OM into MODERA; 'after' puts TOR (a rocky hill, a Dartmoor word) behind it. The Moderator presides over the Church of Scotland's General Assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moderator is the presiding minister of a Presbyterian assembly, a churchman holding high office.

clue.text: Peter, such a saint of the Church of Rome

definitions.text: Peter, such a saint of the Church of Rome

parts.words: Peter, such a saint of the Church of Rome
parts.note: St Peter's basilica in Rome takes its name from the apostle, so Peter is the saint who gives his name to that church

explanation.surface: Saint Peter, revered by the Roman Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of Rome here is the building, St Peter's: the saint is the one it is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone giving their name to a thing, as the apostle does to the Roman basilica.

clue.text: Lars Porsena bade his messengers summon his

definitions.text: Lars Porsena bade his messengers summon his

parts.words: Lars Porsena bade his messengers summon his
parts.note: completes a line from Macaulay's poem Horatius, where the Etruscan king sends riders out to gather his forces

explanation.surface: An Etruscan king sends out messengers to call up his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay's Horatius: 'Lars Porsena of Clusium ... bade his messengers ride forth ... to summon his array.' The missing last word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Military forces drawn up in order, the sense Macaulay's poem uses for the king's assembled host.

clue.text: Somehow manage a work period

definitions.meaning: to ... for oneself is to get by however one can
a stint of working hours, such as a night stint at a factory

explanation.definitionFit: To get by by one's own means, as in fending for oneself; also a block of working hours in a rota.

clue.text: Wagner's Ring for one-to Grey total disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An opera cycle proves a complete failure for a man called Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring cycle is four operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetralogy is a set of four related works, and the Ring has four operas.

clue.text: Like many old sailors, claim to be given no rest

definitions.meaning: many sailors of the past were forced into the navy by press gangs

definitions.text: claim to be given no rest
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a person saying they are hard-pushed and busy

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as I'M PRESSED, what a harried person might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ganged into naval service, as many sailors once were; split in two it says 'I am being hurried'.

clue.text: It records the travels of Shanks's pony

definitions.text: It records the travels of Shanks's pony

parts.words: It records the travels of Shanks's pony
parts.note: Shanks's pony is British slang for going on foot, so this gadget logs how far a walker has gone

explanation.surface: A device that logs a horse's journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Shanks's pony is a British phrase for one's own legs, so walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts a walker's steps and so the distance covered on foot.

clue.text: Steve Rice may be too reserved

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A man called Steve Rice might be excessively shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretive means inclined to conceal things, more reserved than is usual.

clue.text: Opportune to let mildew run riot

indicators.note: running riot means going wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Damp conditions are just right to let mould spread wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at exactly the right moment, a synonym.

clue.text: Sir Henry ignored in print

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood, the conductor who founded the Proms
to cut someone is to ignore them deliberately

explanation.surface: A knight is snubbed in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood founded the London Promenade Concerts; to cut someone is to snub them.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a carved wooden block.

clue.text: Implied one's in diplomacy

indicators.note: the numeral one is placed inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A suggestion made by someone well versed in diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being stated, a synonym of unspoken or implied.

clue.text: Pachyderms get uneasy rest around the river

indicators.note: around means the jumbled word encloses the river
uneasy means unsettled, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the Usk, a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Elephants sleep badly beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasy' rearranges REST to TERS; 'around' puts it round USK, a Welsh river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuskers are elephants or boars with long tusks, thick-skinned animals.

clue.text: An amateur all-rounder returns for City

indicators.note: returns means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator
O, a letter that is round all over

explanation.surface: An amateur cricketer who bats and bowls comes back to play in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A + HAM + O into OMAHA, the city in Nebraska. An all-rounder in cricket bats and bowls; here it is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Cancel article from periodical

indicators.note: from means the article is taken away out of the publication word

parts.note: an annual is a yearly publication
A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor drops a piece from a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, a synonym of cancel.

clue.text: Help stamp out these leaflets

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: An appeal for help in stamping out the distribution of handbills.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamphlets are small unbound booklets or leaflets, a synonym.

clue.text: Soft sanctimonious article, nothing to it

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
an, the indefinite article
O, zero

explanation.surface: A gentle, preachy essay with no substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction for playing softly.

clue.text: " Paradise Regained " when 'e's in this asylum

definitions.text: " Paradise Regained " when 'e's in this asylum

parts.words: " Paradise Regained " when 'e's in this asylum
parts.note: put a dropped-aitch E into a place of refuge and it becomes the word for paradise

explanation.surface: A Milton title, with a Cockney inmate at a lunatic asylum.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's poem title is a pun: add E to the refuge and you get the word for paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a safe place of shelter, an asylum or refuge.

clue.text: Letter in agreement

definitions.meaning: a letter of the alphabet that is not a vowel, such as B or T
being in harmony or accord with something

explanation.definitionFit: A non-vowel letter of the alphabet; also an adjective for harmony, as in being consistent with.

clue.text: Sister of Milton's verse

parts.note: in Milton's ode At a Solemn Music, two harmonious sisters are named, and verse is one of the pair

explanation.surface: A female relative of the poet Milton, or a sister mentioned in his poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's At a Solemn Music begins 'Blest pair of Sirens ... Sphere-born harmonious sisters, Voice and Verse.'
explanation.definitionFit: Milton pairs song and poetry as sisters, the singing one being the spoken or sung sound of a person.

clue.text: Agree with old Hanoi leader to indicate a view?

parts.note: accounts tally when they agree
Ho Chi Minh, former leader of North Vietnam, whose capital was Hanoi

explanation.surface: A diplomat agrees with the former Vietnamese leader so as to signal his opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' looks like an opinion, but it is a sighting: the hunter's cry when the fox is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry raised in fox hunting when the quarry is sighted.

clue.text: Comparatively malodorous, one of these soldiers

definitions.text: Comparatively malodorous, one of these soldiers

parts.words: Comparatively malodorous, one of these soldiers
parts.note: the comparative of rank, smelly, names one soldier, so a group of private soldiers from the ranks is the plural

explanation.surface: Some soldiers smell worse than others.
explanation.walkthrough: A RANKER is a soldier from the ranks, and 'ranker' is also 'more rank', i.e. smellier.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers serving in the ranks rather than as officers, and singly each is smellier than another.
